newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BLYVOOR BUYS WESTERN DEEP TRIBUTE AREA.
newsitem.headline: BLYVOOR BUYS WESTERN DEEP TRIBUTE AREA.

text.p: Blyvooruitzicht Gold Mining Co Ltd has acquired the Carbon Leader Reef tribute area of Western Deep Levels for 25.5 million rand in cash, Blyvoor said on Wednesday.

A company statement said the acquisition and extension of the tribute would allow Blyoor to rationalise its operating shafts, reduce its operating costs and give greater flexibility to its ore reserve management.
Blyvoor has been mining the tribute area on a royalty basis since 1992.

"The combination of the current tribute area and the extension will increase the total area to 136.39 hectares containing 3.9 million tonnes of ore, at an in situ grade of 11.2 grammes per tonne," the statement said.
"This means that Blyvoor is effectively paying $4.04 per in situ ounce of gold."
The company said it planned to produce 585,934 ounces of gold from the area and the payback period was estimated at four years.
It did not say how the acquisition would be financed, but Blyvoor raised 40 million rand with a rights issue earlier this year.
Blyvoor is managed by Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd, while Western Deep is managed by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd .
The company said there would be no material effect on the net asset value of either Blyvoor or Western Deep.

"The effects of the transaction on the earnings of Blyvoor for the 12-month period ended June 30, 1996, assuming the transaction had become effective on June 30, 1995, will be to decrease the loss per share from 0.3 cents per share to 0.14 cents per share.
"There will be no material effect on the earnings per share of Western Deep," it said.
